Combining strong commercial judgement with data-led decision-making, you will identify opportunities, drive performance and lead cross-functional teams to deliver growth.</p> <h2>The Details</h2> <ul> <li>Own UK website performance across revenue, traffic, conversion, AOV, margin and profitability.</li> <li>Set and deliver the UK ecommerce trading strategy, translating business targets into clear priorities and action plans.</li> <li>Drive onsite trading and optimisation across merchandising, navigation, search, landing pages and promotional activity.</li> <li>Manage pricing and promotional investment, balancing revenue growth, margin and customer experience.</li> <li>Lead forecasting and performance reviews, identifying risks, opportunities and actions to maximise trading performance.</li> <li>Use customer insight, competitor activity and market trends to inform commercial decisions and identify growth opportunities.</li> <li>Partner with Marketing, CRM, Brand, Product, UX, Technology, Supply Chain and Finance to deliver the UK growth agenda.</li> <li>Drive improvements across the customer journey, increasing conversion, basket size, retention and customer lifetime value.</li> <li>Lead testing and optimisation initiatives, using clear hypotheses and measurable commercial outcomes.</li> <li>Champion AI, automation and analytics to improve decision-making, efficiency and trading effectiveness.</li> <li>Influence senior stakeholders and hold cross-functional teams accountable for delivering commercial priorities.</li> </ul> <h3>What We Are Looking For</h3> <ul> <li>Significant experience in ecommerce, digital trading or online retail, ideally within a fast-paced DTC or consumer business.</li> <li>Proven track record of owning website performance and delivering profitable commercial growth.</li> <li>Strong understanding of ecommerce trading metrics, including revenue, conversion, AOV, margin and customer lifetime value.</li> <li>Experience developing and executing trading strategies and onsite optimisation plans.</li> <li>Strong commercial judgement, with the ability to balance growth, profitability and customer experience.</li> <li>Highly analytical and data-driven, able to turn insight into clear commercial actions.</li> <li>Proactive and autonomous, with a strong bias for action and personal accountability.</li> <li>Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and lead cross-functional teams.</li> <li>Experience in testing, optimisation and continuous improvement.</li> <li>Confident using BI and ecommerce analytics tools, with an interest in leveraging AI and automation to improve performance.</li> <li>Clear communicator, comfortable challenging thinking and driving decisions at pace.</li> </ul> <h2>What’s in It for Me?</h2> <h3>Career Development</h3> <ul> <li> <p>Access bespoke development programmes designed by our in-house Learning & Development team.</p> </li> <li> <p>Develop your expertise through our upskilling programme, delivered in partnership with an industry-leading training provider.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>Enhanced Leave</h3> <ul> <li> <p>25 days’ annual leave plus bank holidays.</p> </li> <li> <p>Enjoy your birthday off, on us!</p> </li> <li> <p>Enhanced maternity and paternity pay, depending on length of service.</p> </li> <li> <p>Up to 10 days’ compassionate leave.</p> </li> <li> <p>Option to buy up to 3 additional days of annual leave each year.</p> </li> <li> <p>Unlock 2 days of volunteer leave after 12 months.</p> </li> </ul> our Security and Workplace teams.</li> </ul> <ul> <li>Contribute to root cause analysis for recurring and high-impact incidents, and capture the detail the team needs to automate repetitive work.</li> <li>Write and maintain knowledge base articles and runbooks in Confluence so employees can self-serve and colleagues can pick up where you left off.</li> <li>Explore new tools and approaches, and tell title: Data Architect
description: 🍊Our mission Great science regularly stalls in the clinic, not because the science is wrong, but because the company behind it lacks the capital, infrastructure, or focus to take it all the way through. Today’s clinical-stage biopharma model is broken, and as a result promising treatments never reach patients. Our mission is to fix this: we’re building the next generation of biopharma by in-licensing clinical-stage therapeutic assets and developing them through Lindus Health’s integrated, technology-first clinical trial infrastructure. We’re a new initiative, but we’re building on a proven foundation - the same infrastructure that has delivered 82% of Lindus Health’s sponsor trials on or ahead of timeline, across 40+ completed trials across the US and Europe. We’re in-licensing 5-7 clinical-stage, typically Phase-2-ready assets, funded directly from Lindus Health’s balance sheet. We’re targeting deal close on our first assets through 2026, with first trials launching in H1 2027. 🍊About the role The Data Architect owns assigned studies end-to-end, taking full responsibility for both the design of the database on Citrus and the quality of the data it produces, from study planning through database lock. The role designs with the final analysis in mind, writes code where manual review would slow delivery, and designs the edit checks and validation that prevent issues before they make their way downstream. The Data Architect is the technical and data lead for assigned studies and works with Clinical Operations, Biostatistics, Programme Directors, and Product to ensure each study captures the data its scientific objectives require. One person owns the database from study planning through lock, so the design and the data it produces never drift apart. The role also shapes how data delivery on Citrus develops, identifying where manual work can be automated. 🍊About you You have around 5+ years of experience across clinical data management and/or trial platform design, with hands-on involvement in study setup, data review, and database lock You can design a study's data capture on an EDC platform and define its specification: you understand edit checks and validation, and you can see how a design decision today could become a data quality problem later You work with data programmatically, or are ready to build that skill quickly: Python, R, or SQL are used daily in this role, and you are expected to learn them on the job if you do not already have them You have working knowledge of CDISC standards, particularly CDASH, with SDTM familiarity a plus, and you design with analysis-ready data in mind You have experience with external data transfers and reconciliation You understand GCP, ICH E6 and 21 CFR Part 11 and apply them in day-to-day decisions You apply AI and automation responsibly to improve the quality and speed of data work in a regulated setting You have a track record of working well across functions, especially Clinical Operations, Biostatistics, Programme Directors, and Product You thrive in a startup environment that challenges the norms of typical biotechs, with high agency and a bias for action You are passionate about our mission: changing how the healthcare industry operates and how new health treatments are developed 🍊What you’ll focus on Own your assigned studies end-to-end, from defining critical data items and the data management plan through to database lock Own the design of your studies on Citrus, utilizing AI combined with your expert review to translate protocol requirements into a specification and edit check logic that capture clean, analysis-ready data, and sign off that the design meets the protocol before go-live Assess feasibility and flag complexity and risk early, where a design choice could affect data integrity, participant safety or study endpoints Manage the full query lifecycle from generation through resolution, working directly with sites Lead proactive, risk-based data review, automated where possible, to keep key study milestones on track, building repeatable checks rather than one-off reports Use scripting and AI tooling day-to-day to automate data review, flag anomalies, and surface issues earlier, applied responsibly within validation, GCP and 21 CFR Part 11 expectations Own fixes and change requests on your own studies during conduct, assessing their impact and the level of testing and sign-off required Perform ongoing safety data review and facilitate medical coding (MedDRA, WHODrug) with the medical team Build reports using programmatic data access (Python, R, SQL), delivered accurately and on schedule Conduct all activities in line with relevant regulations and Lindus SOPs, keep study documentation to a standard that holds up under audit or inspection, and support auditors and inspectors on your studies where needed Report bugs and usability issues, and feed operational insight back to Product to improve how Citrus supports data delivery 🍊 What we offer (US) Make an impact across all areas of our business and fix one of the world's most broken industries. About Kaluza Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future. Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life. With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen. Where in the world of Kaluza will I be working? You'll be joining the Information & Cyber Security team, a core part of our Platform & Security Engineering organisation. Security at Kaluza isn't a silo — you'll work closely with colleagues across security engineering, identity and access management, platform engineering and enterprise technical services. As the Security GRC Lead, you will serve as the accountable operational owner for Kaluza’s Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance capability. You will establish and maintain a unified Common Control Framework, lead regulatory and framework readiness (including SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, and ISO 22301), and work with engineering teams to demonstrate effective implementation of controls. A core focus of this role is acting as the primary information security bridge to Kaluza’s central Risk & Compliance team. You will closely collaborate with them to assess the impact of evolving security and privacy regulations, ensuring regulatory risks are clearly quantified, actionable, and seamlessly integrated into the wider enterprise risk framework. What you will be doing Regulatory Impact & Horizon Scanning: Collaborate closely with the Risk & Compliance team to monitor, evaluate, and interpret emerging regulatory changes in the information security, privacy, and critical infrastructure domains. Security Impact Assessments: Translate complex regulatory developments into actionable security control requirements and risk assessments for Kaluza, specifically covering: Sector & Critical Infrastructure Regulations: NIS2, AESCSF, NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF), and the UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill. Emerging Tech & Governance Standards: AI management and governance expectations (ISO 42001). Enterprise Risk Integration: Partner with Risk & Compliance to ensure security and resilience risks, control gaps, and regulatory exposures seamlessly flow into and align with the enterprise risk management (ERM) framework. Maintain high data accuracy across the security risk register to support board-level visibility. Common Control Framework: Design, build, and maintain a single Common Control Framework (anchored initially on ISO 27001 Annex A) mapped across all regulatory, framework, and client contractual requirements. Standards & Policy Suite: Help continuously improve Kaluza's security policy and standards library. Continuous Control Monitoring: Shift Kaluza from point-in-time evidence gathering to automated control monitoring using commercial GRC platforms (e.g., Vanta), making audit readiness a natural byproduct of daily operations. SOC 2 Type 2 Programme: Lead the gap assessment, control build-out, and sustained observation period required for Kaluza’s SOC 2 Type 2 commitment. Standards Maintenance: Oversee continuous alignment with ISO 27001 and ISO 22301 to prevent posture drift between annual audit cycles. Governance Reporting: Draft security reporting for internal leadership committees and forums, ensuring alignment with enterprise-wide reporting standards set by Risk & Compliance. Client Security Assurance: Own client security reporting commitments and streamline response workflows for client questionnaires and external audits. External Partner Coordination: Direct and manage external GRC consultants (e.g., Cydea) to execute audit operations and supplier assessments efficiently. What you will have Core Framework Expertise: Hands-on experience implementing and managing ISO 27001, ISO 22301, and SOC 2 Type 2 frameworks. Regulatory Horizon Scanning: Sound understanding of UK/EU cybersecurity laws, critical infrastructure mandates (e.g., NIS2, CSRB, CAF), and emerging tech governance. Tooling & Risk Management: Experience working with automated GRC platforms (e.g., Vanta, Drata) and managing risk registers aligned with enterprise risk taxonomies. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Demonstrated experience partnering with enterprise Risk, Legal, or Compliance teams to analyze and operationalize complex regulatory requirements. We would still encourage you to apply even if you don’t have experience of all of the above - we look for potential as much as skills fit. Leadership & communication You’ll be… Strongly aligned with the principle of "business value over compliance-for-its-own-sake", focusing on practical, lean governance rather than administrative overhead. Able to build strong bridges across central Risk & Compliance, technical engineering teams, senior leadership, and enterprise clients. A proactive leader comfortable establishing an integrated GRC capability from design through to execution. A pragmatic decision-maker who takes into account the short & long-term commercial, people & process costs and consequences of those decisions Accomplished at influencing (within teams, as well as upwards and outwards), using a mixture of communications skills Skilled in bringing alignment, clarity of thought and direction to information security, compliance and engineering challenges Why Join Kaluza in This Role? Strategic Enterprise Impact: You will shape how security governance interfaces with central Risk & Compliance, directly influencing Kaluza's posture across international energy markets. Unlocking Technical Innovation: Your work takes compliance administration away from senior engineers, enabling them to focus on core platform innovation like AI security architecture and multi-tenant scaling. You’ll leverage AI-assisted tooling to synthesize and reconcile control evidence from multiple operational systems with human oversight, helping us accelerate & innovate within the compliance domain. Growth Capability: As the accountable owner of GRC, you will establish the foundation and build the business case for expanding the security GRC team as Kaluza scales. Our Values Five values guide how we work at Kaluza: Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale. Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes. Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say. Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego. Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives. Our Perks Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% [of salary] to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget Climate: Furthr, our climate action app Come as you are We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you. Role purpose The Senior Analyst, Underwriting Quality Control (QC) will establish and continually improve a consistent, risk-based quality control framework for work completed by Underwriters. The role will build on existing QC practices and tools, tailoring them to the Underwriting lifecycle, products, risk decisions and operating model. The role provides an objective, evidence-led check that underwriting assessments and outcomes are complete, consistent, appropriately documented and aligned with internal policy, procedures and applicable requirements. It will turn review results into clear management information, actionable feedback, targeted training and measurable improvements in underwriting quality. This is a hands-on role. The Senior Analyst will conduct QC reviews, maintain the framework and reporting, follow findings through to verified remediation, and work with Underwriters and leaders to address recurring gaps. The role reports to the Director of Underwriting and influences quality across the function without replacing the Underwriter’s decision-making accountability. Key responsibilities Build and own the QC framework Assess existing QC materials, controls, data and workflows; identify what should be retained, improved or introduced for Underwriting. Design, document and implement an Underwriting-specific QC framework, including scope, risk-based sampling, review cadence, test scripts, scoring and severity definitions, evidence standards, escalation routes, dispute handling, calibration and remediation expectations. Tailor testing to the relevant underwriting stages, products, merchant and business models, risk tiers and applicable regional requirements. Define practical service levels and ownership for review, feedback, acknowledgement, remediation, re-review and closure, agreeing these with Underwriting leadership. Establish appropriate governance and records so that QC decisions and remediation are traceable and ready for internal or external review. Perform and calibrate QC reviews Review completed underwriting cases and test whether the case record is complete, and appropriately documented. Depending on case scope, this may include business model products, services and geographies; ownership, control and beneficial ownership; company and identity evidence; KYC/KYB and screening outcomes; licences and regulatory status; financial and operational evidence and accurate system records. Identify missing, inconsistent, stale or insufficient evidence, and opportunities to improve decision quality. Drive remediation and constructive challenge Communicate findings promptly, clearly and fairly to the relevant Underwriter and manager, with evidence and an actionable explanation of what needs to change. Track acknowledgement, corrective action and deadlines; proactively chase overdue responses and escalate unresolved or repeat issues. Work with Underwriters and leaders to understand root causes and ensure remediation addresses the underlying issue, not only the individual case. Reporting, insight and continuous improvement Produce regular, accurate QC reporting for Underwriting leadership, with clear commentary on coverage, pass and defect rates, severity, recurring themes, remediation status, turnaround and trends by relevant team, workflow, product or risk segment. Support internal audit, Compliance, Risk and other assurance requests by providing accurate QC records and explaining methodology and outcomes. Build underwriting capability Identify capability gaps from QC findings and partner with Underwriting leaders and relevant subject-matter experts to design and deliver focused training, coaching and practical guidance. What Success Looks Like The ideal candidate is a rigorous and constructive quality professional who can build a practical control framework, apply it consistently and influence experienced Underwriters. They combine sound KYC/KYB judgement with strong analytical and reporting skills, confidence in following through on remediation, and the ability to turn case-level observations into improvements across a regional operation. Essential Significant experience in underwriting, merchant due diligence, AML/KYC/KYB, onboarding, financial crime operations, quality control, quality assurance or a related risk function within financial services, payments or fintech. Practical understanding of UK and EEA due diligence requirements, with familiarity across the US, Canada, Singapore, Hong Kong, UAE, Australia and New Zealand; ability to recognise jurisdictional differences and escalate interpretation questions appropriately. Demonstrated ability to design, implement or materially improve a QC, QA, control testing or file review framework. Strong reporting and data skills, including spreadsheets, pivot tables and clear management reporting; experience with Looker dashboard or business intelligence tools is an advantage. Use of AI is a plus. Effective stakeholder management and influencing skills, including the persistence to chase remediation and escalate overdue or repeat issues appropriately. Experience delivering training or coaching based on quality control findings. Nice to Have Direct exposure to underwriting or due diligence in a merchant acquiring setting. Familiarity with case management and CRM tools,dashboard platforms. A relevant degree or equivalent practical experience; recognised AML, financial crime or compliance qualifications (for example ACAMS or ICA) are beneficial but not mandatory. description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>Our Mission:</strong></p> <p>6sense's mission is to multiply what matters: growth, retention, and efficiency.  We envision a future where companies, teams and people reach their full potential.</p> <p><strong>Our People:</strong></p> <p>People are the heart and soul of 6sense. We serve with passion and purpose. We live by our Being 6sense values of Win as One Team, Stay Curious, Do The Right Thing, Own the Outcome, and Create Belonging.  Every 6sensor plays a part in deﬁning the future of our industry-leading technology.  6sense is a place where difference-makers roll up their sleeves, take risks, act with integrity, and measure success by the value we create for our customers.  We want 6sense to be the best chapter of your career. </p></div><p>The Role: Imagine selling a solution that will predict for your customers (with an 85% accuracy) who is going to buy, what they’ll buy and when.  As a Strategic Account Executive at 6sense, you’ll be an instrumental player to our growth as we build upon the success we’ve had delivering predictions for enterprises like Cisco, Centrify, Dell, Qlik, and Oracle.  We will trust you to evangelize 6sense, run your business like a CEO, and consistently exceed quarterly and annual targets.  This is not your average start-up; you’ll be closing large deals.  And you’ll be rewarded very well for doing so.<br><br>The Fit: We’re looking for hunters who not only have a track record of being the best of the best, closing big deals and passion for fundamentally changing B2B marketing and sales, but can also think critically about driving customer growth and building our sales organization.  This is a unique opportunity to help shape and accelerate our success.<br><br>Here are the traits you exhibit;</p> <ul> <li>Intrinsic drive to be successful, love to win – You’ll take initiative to figure it out, are motivated to do your absolute best work. description: <div> <div> <h2>About the Role </h2> <p>You’ll help specialists shape requirements, design margins and acceptance criteria across silicon, package, PCB and system boundaries. Your team’s constraints and verification evidence will help design owners make informed trade-offs before problems become harder to resolve.</p> <p>You’ll line-manage engineers, shape their development, agree achievable delivery commitments, and plan for tools, licences and compute capacity. You’ll coordinate analysis and hardware correlation, ensuring discrepancies receive specialist attention and integrity issues reach review and closure.</p> <p>The methods and knowledge your team builds will outlast individual designs, strengthening how Graphcore approaches future signal and power challenges. Grow your leadership across interconnected engineering disciplines, combining people development with judgement that influences hardware from architecture to bring-up.</p> <h2>The team and culture</h2> <p>Signal and power integrity specialists retain technical ownership, rather than relying on one person to solve every problem. You’ll connect their work with design, firmware, test, bring-up and manufacturing colleagues.</p> <p>Programme management owns the integrated plan. You’ll lead this London-based team through its next phase of growth, helping build and maintain a reliable, high-performance, multi-cloud and multi-region platform. Your goal is to maximise the impact of the team in alignment with the department and company objectives. Improving scheduling and availability: Oversee Kubernetes-based infrastructure and queuing and scheduling systems, enabling workloads to use the right resources across heterogeneous GPU environments. Planning capacity and cost: Partner with stakeholders and cloud providers on compute and storage forecasts, accounting for resource lead times, performance requirements and cost trade-offs. You can reason about availability, capacity, performance and cost across complex cloud infrastructure, including the interaction between compute, storage and data movement. You understand large-scale GPU compute infrastructure for machine learning training or inference and the operational challenges of scaling beyond small GPU deployments. You can earn engineers’ trust through sound technical judgement without needing to be the team’s primary individual contributor. You are able to work from our London office and lead a team based there. If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement. More about Wayve: 🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines. Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility. How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working: Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. title: Lead Analytics Engineer - Finance Data (FinOps)
description: About Finom Finom is growing fast, and Finance needs data that grows with it. As our Lead Analytics Engineer for Finance, you'll be the data partner for treasury, reconciliation and accounting. You'll also support our corporate finance and investor reporting work together with the team's existing data partner. You'll build and scale the data model behind these areas, set standards, integrate the systems Finance relies on and bring in automation, including agents, where it saves real work This isn't a "build what's in the ticket" role. You'll learn how Finance works and why, understand where the value is, and work with the team on how their processes run, proposing improvements and the data and tools to support them. You'll report to the Head of Central Data What You Will Be Doing - Partner with the Treasury, Reconciliation and Accounting teams on their processes, priorities and how data supports them. - Build out treasury data: positions, cash flows and liquidity, as trusted data products the team can rely on day to day. - Build and scale reconciliation, so that matching, breaks and exceptions are handled systematically rather than by hand. - Support Accounting with the data, checks and integrations behind their close and day-to-day work. - Support our corporate finance data partner on corporate finance and investor reporting, working from one shared model and set of definitions. - Design and evolve the Finance data model, entities and metrics, with tests, lineage and documentation, so the team can reuse and extend them. - Set data standards and quality checks for Finance data, and build integrations with the systems Finance uses. - Bring automation and agents into Finance workflows where they remove recurring manual work. - Look at how Finance processes run today, identify what can work better and connect each piece of data work to its business cost and value. How We Work You'll have high autonomy. You choose the tools and the approach, including trialling new vendors and open-source solutions. Sign-off is needed in two cases. Priorities are set by final business impact. Who You Are - You've worked in or closely with Finance: in a finance team, as a finance data partner, or in data work centred on treasury, reconciliation, accounting or FP&A. - You understand how a finance function works: the close, cash and liquidity, reconciliations and the reports that come out of them. - You write expert SQL and have strong dimensional or semantic data modelling skills. - You've built metrics and data products that other teams depend on. - You have ETL and data warehouse or lakehouse experience, including onboarding sources end to end. - You choose precision over speed when the two conflict. - You work like a consultant to the business: you understand how a process works, propose solutions and frame them in terms of business value. title: Innovative Project Planner (Data Centres / Buildings / High-tech / Infrastructure) - UK (Hybrid)
description: Are you a bit tired of the standard, old-fashioned way of doing things in the construction industry? Do you get deep satisfaction from making things run more efficiently using a good dose of common sense and maybe a bit of technology? Have you always cared about the importance of proper planning and the connection between the schedule and the real, day-to-day delivery of the job? Have you ever wanted to work a bit more flexibly but still be hands-on in construction and improving the industry? Sounds like a dream. Well, it isn’t. It’s quite real! Read on. ____________________________________________________________ We are Laminar Projects! If you’ve already heard about us, you’re probably reading this because you’re tired of the typical, chaotic ways of doing things in construction. But in case you haven’t, we’re a high-end project management consultancy and tech developer with a focus on upgrading the way construction projects are delivered. Improving construction strengthens the very foundation of human civilisation. ( Check out our short film about it. ) We bring transparency and control to projects through a pragmatic mix of the latest tech, our own processes, and a big dose of common sense. We then take our deep understanding of these projects and we invest heavily into developing the digital solutions that anyone can use to deliver their projects better. ( Check out Shape, our construction management tech, to see what we’re doing.) The core of all this is our true secret sauce: our people. We only recruit the very best, both in capability and personality. We’re deeply focused on designing a new type of organisation that’s optimised for the flourishing of the people in the team first and foremost. People who join us develop fast as a whole person in ways they never imagined. ( Read more about our vision and missions .) This approach has allowed us to grow from just two people in 2017 to over 220 today. We have a stable, repeat client base across infrastructure and complex building projects in the UK and internationally, and we’re still growing fast. Joining us isn’t just some “job”. It’s a transformative educational experience. We challenge you to be your best self in all aspects of life. There are many diverse and interesting challenges available. It’s up to you to guide yourself into whichever areas you’re most interested – we’ll enable it. ( Get to know us better by watching a few more of our videos. ) Core values for a good life A life of human flourishing is all about meaningful relationships and challenging yourself to create a positive impact, so our values reflect the four levels of relationships that each of us has: - Grow yourself – your relationship with yourself - Care about people – your relationship with others around you - Execute to greatness – your relationship with your team - Build civilisation – your relationship with humanity and the world We enshrined our values in our vision: We exist so that everyone in our team can flourish in a high-impact community that: - Connects us with meaningful relationships - Inspires us to develop ourselves to become better humans - Empowers us to pursue our own learning adventures By first doing this, we can achieve the highest levels of value for the world. And enable the achievement of our vision through our two missions: - To fully digitalise the construction of human civilisation - To create a new type of organisation that enables human flourishing while delivering a huge positive impact on society ____________________________________________________________ The Role Purpose of the role You’ll be enhancing the delivery of the most complex and interesting projects in the world through the power of project planning to the very highest standards. You’ll devise strategies and tactics to improve the way the project is delivered. You’ll translate this knowledge into a logic-linked plan and analyse it using planning software. Then you’ll use the plan to help the teams understand what to prioritise. Your team This role is part of our Project Management Consultancy team which focuses on: - Understanding what the real problems of projects are - Implementing the best solutions to those problems - Developing scalable best practices, tools and technology More specifically, you’ll be part of our Project Planning Team, who are industry leaders in the planning of complex construction projects. Your initial leader will be one of our planning discipline directors. Your top three objectives 1. To make construction projects deliver to near perfection 2. To create scalable and repeatable solutions to common problems 3. To develop yourself and everyone around you Your top five responsibilities 1. Own the plan: Own the project plan for one or more projects and ensure that the project is working to it effectively. Ensure delays are mitigated and managed commercially 2. Own the outcome: You're responsible for putting in your best effort to ensure the project team’s understanding and focus on the plan – no matter how stubborn they are 3. Report and inform: Provide simple, actionable reports to stakeholders at all levels that help them deliver their part of the project more efficiently and effectively 4. Make scalable solutions : Develop scalable and repeatable best practices and tools in collaboration with the team so that long-term impact is achieved 5. Develop everyone: Maximise the development of your team personally and professionally and educate our clients to improve as well You must have: - A construction engineering background: You have at least 2+ years of experience on construction projects, experience in project planning both software and principles, as well as decent Excel skills, and a strong interest in data - Communication skills: You’re proficient in written and verbal English and have the charisma and influence to get construction people to do new things and take the best approach - Leadership capabilities: You lead yourself proactively and lead others by asking the right questions and challenging them - Impact: You have a track record of making projects and organisations better beyond just doing the basics – implementing scalable, repeatable solutions that had a significant positive impact Laminar isn’t the place for you if any of the following is true: - You want an easy, chilled-out role without much challenge - You like to be the smartest person in the room - You don’t like continuously receiving honest candid feedback - You prefer to do your own thing rather than work with a team ____________________________________________________________ Frequently Asked Questions What kinds of projects would I be working on? It’s common for people to be exposed to several projects in their first year with us. You’ll work on some of the most complex and interesting environments in the world. We’ve delivered over 100 data centres internationally, many of them fast-tracked and multi-package. Our teams have supported flagship infrastructure programmes like HS2 through integrated planning and digital delivery, contributed to over $30bn in power generation and transmission projects, and played a key role in the development of high-containment labs and R&D campuses for some of the world’s most advanced industrial and life sciences clients. You might find yourself working in sectors such as data centres , infrastructure (including defense, rail, and highways), high tech (such as advanced manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, and semiconductors), or complex building projects . These aren’t hands-off assignments. They’re dynamic, hands-on environments designed for people who want to be challenged. We bring back the lessons from every project to help our team grow and deliver the highest levels of value. ( Check out our case stories .) Who are our clients? Major owners/operators and main contractors with project values between £1m and £1bn+ globally. Where would I be working? One week you might be working from home. The next, you might travel to the site to meet the construction teams and help organise them. Maybe you’ll pop into our London office for a workshop or a beer. Maybe you’ll fly out to exotic (and sometimes not!) locations in Europe or the Middle East to visit clients. It really depends on what you want to get involved in and what fits with your life. How does what I do connect with the long-term impact on the construction industry? You’re tasked with understanding and solving common problems. We don’t want to reinvent the wheel every time, so you’ll be responsible for documenting new solutions and evolving ones we’ve developed. This goes into our knowledge repository, which we’re going to open source to the industry. The knowledge you capture will be used by us to build new products. You’ll constantly test those products in the field, so we can rapidly iterate and improve them for anyone in the industry to use. ____________________________________________________________ Benefits The standard stuff: - Health Insurance Scheme. Comprehensive private health coverage – for you and your family. Because your well-being is our priority - Pension Scheme. What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together. About the role We're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join our Bank Infrastructure team at Pleo. This team builds and maintains the payment rails that power Pleo's money movement, integrating with banks and payment partners to handle inbound and outbound bank transfers reliably and at scale. You'll be working on some of the most critical systems at Pleo: the infrastructure that guarantees that each financial transaction, whether incoming, outgoing, or internal, is processed and settled with absolute accuracy, on time, and with the resilience to recover gracefully when things go wrong. If you're excited by the challenge of building highly reliable financial systems and want to work in a culture that values transparency, collaboration, and engineering excellence, this role is for you. What you’ll be doing As a Senior Backend Engineer on Bank Infrastructure, you will: Design, build, and maintain integrations with banks and payment partners across multiple payment schemes (SEPA, Faster Payments, SWIFT, and others). Own the reliability and correctness of inbound and outbound payment flows, including reconciliation, settlement, and exception handling. Architect systems that are resilient to partner outages, network failures, and edge cases inherent in financial messaging. Lead initiatives to improve system observability, fault tolerance, and operational excellence across payment rails. Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including compliance, finance operations, and product to evolve Pleo's payment capabilities. Participate in code reviews, post-mortems, and provide mentorship to other engineers. Proactively address technical debt and guide the team through technical challenges and migrations. What you bring You'll thrive in this role if you have: Hands-on experience building payment integrations, bank APIs, payment scheme integrations, or financial messaging formats (ISO 20022, SWIFT, SEPA, Faster Payments, or similar). Strong understanding of payment flows end-to-end: payment initiation, routing, reconciliation, settlement, and exception/failure handling. Experience designing and operating highly available, resilient distributed systems with robust error recovery and observability. Expertise in server-side development, ideally Kotlin or Java, with strong experience in microservices and distributed systems. Proficiency with relational databases (PostgreSQL), cloud environments (AWS, Kubernetes), and observability tooling (e.g. Grafana). Awareness of payment compliance and regulatory considerations (e.g. AML, sanctions screening, PSD2) is a plus. Understanding of safeguarding of customer funds and the impact of money movement pipelines. Strong problem-solving skills and experience owning production payment systems through incidents and operational complexity. High proficiency with AI-enhanced development tools (such as GitHub Copilot or Claude) as integrated partners for system design, documentation, and code generation. Willingness to deepen your AI fluency as Pleo scales AI adoption across engineering. We're building a culture where thoughtful AI use for delivery velocity and quality. Proven ability to structure complex engineering problems for AI collaboration, including writing precise specifications, validating generated outputs, and iterative development. A proactive drive to expand your AI fluency as we scale adoption to enhance delivery velocity and maintain high engineering quality across our organisation. A collaborative mindset and the ability to mentor and upskill teammates. Who you’ll be working with and reporting to You'll report to the Engineering Manager for Bank Infrastructure and work closely with cross-functional teams spanning product, finance operations, compliance, and other engineering squads within Pleo's Payments organisation. Bank Infrastructure is foundational to nearly everything Pleo does, your work will have direct dependencies with and from Card Infrastructure, Credit, and beyond. You'll collaborate with partners across the business to shape how Pleo moves money reliably at scale. How you’ll develop in this role In your first six months at Pleo, you'll: Get deep into Pleo's payment rail architecture, understanding how inbound and outbound bank payment flows are built, monitored, and operated. Take ownership of meaningful initiatives in the bank integration or payment operations domain and drive them from design to production. Build relationships across the engineering organisation, contributing to code reviews and technical discussions beyond your immediate team. Grow your expertise in high-reliability, mission-critical financial infrastructure while contributing to Pleo's broader engineering culture. We're committed to supporting your growth, whether through expanding your payment systems expertise, stepping into broader architectural influence, or taking on technical leadership responsibilities as Pleo scales. Show me the benefits! 💳 Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!) 🍜 Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office 🏥 Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis 🌴 We offer 25 days of holiday + your public holidays 🏠 For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options 🏖️ Option to purchase 5 additional days of holiday through a salary sacrifice ❤️‍🩹 We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far 👶 Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work The interview process We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows: Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background. Coding Interview (Multiple choice) System Design (whiteboarding session) Engineering Mananeer Behavioural Interview Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success! Last time we hired this role, we received hundreds of applicants but could only speak with so many. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include: CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background! Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process. title: Talent community lead
description: About the role We're hiring a Founder Community Lead to build and run the top of our founder funnel. You'll make sure that every new venture we start has strong prospective founders already engaged before it needs one. Founders Factory builds companies with corporate partners. Next year, we're aiming for 25 approved ventures in the next 12 months, and each venture needs a founder who pitches at the investment committee alongside our venture design team. You'll own our Founder Bench: a small, high-quality community of pre-vetted founders, matched to the sectors and founder profiles our ventures need. You'll fill it through sourcing and partnerships, and keep it active through four events a quarter. You'll sit in the talent team to help matching founders to ventures. What you'll do: Pipeline building: Build a steady flow of experienced founders, operators and domain experts in our partners' focus areas. Run first conversations, write short founder notes, and tag each person by founder archetype, sector, stage and availability. Share our standard founder deal with each person when they join the bench, so terms are clear before anyone commits time. Build referral routes with our portfolio founders, investors, operator communities and university spinout offices. Events: Sector founder drinks: 12–15 founders and operators around a theme from our partner's focus areas. Weekly Open studio office hours: a look at the problems we're working on, so prospective founders can see what building with us is like. Partner event: co-hosted with a feeder programme with a select group of universities Bench gathering: for founders already on the bench, to keep them engaged between ventures with managing a Slack or Whatsapp community or newsletters Engagement: Keep the founder data accurate, with every founder's archetype, sector, availability and last contact up to date in our tracker. Keep founders engaged with regular updates, intros and early sight of new themes, so they're ready when a venture starts. Give the talent team a ready longlist of 5–8 founders for each new venture within its first two weeks. Report monthly on bench size, quality, diversity and how bench founders move through to trials and selection. Who you are: 3+ years in founder-facing work: VC platform or scouting, an accelerator or founder programme, startup community building, or founding a company yourself. A network among founders and operators that you can open up quickly, and the instinct to grow it. The ability to sell an unusual offer: building a venture we've designed with a corporate partner, rather than your own idea. Disciplined pipeline habits, keeping a CRM or tracker accurate across hundreds of relationships. A real commitment to building diverse founder pipelines, and experience doing it. Nice to have Knowledge of, or a network in, healthcare, deep tech or B2B sectors. Experience working with corporate partners or in corporate venturing. Familiarity with Airtable or similar tools. What you'll do Shape the product from zero to MVP. We ship a proof of concept every week. The first MVP lands in December, the second in January. There are no product managers. The core flows and the way the product feels are yours to set. Define how our users interact with agents. By voice and through interfaces that generate themselves. And how the agent earns enough trust to move users money. Prototype and ship in code. You build your designs with coding agents and ship them with the iOS engineers. The code is the deliverable. Stay close to users, every week. You're in the user conversations. You turn what you hear into what you build, and you push back when a brief isn't ready. Craft the details. Flows, interaction design, and visual polish, down to the micro-interactions and signature patterns. What we're looking for 4+ years designing end-to-end on tier-1, design-led, mobile-first consumer apps. A design engineer. You build with coding agents to multiply your output, not to replace craft. Obsessive about small details. You sweat the 1px difference and care about every transition and haptic. You start from the user's problem and make trade-offs explicit. You've taken on more scope, faster than your peers. Curious, self-directed, and excited by the ambiguity of building from zero. Even better if you… Have worked in fintech or wealth. Have designed agent chat or generative UI. Have taken a product from 0 to 1 at an early-stage company. How we work Customer obsession. Everything starts with one question: who are we building it for? If we don't know who they are and what they need, we go and talk to them. Then we build with conviction. Speed. We ship and iterate every week. Something great today beats something perfect next month. Intense, but healthy. High bar. There's always more work than people, and we set the bar high on purpose. Ownership. Real ownership from day one. In person. Five days a week in the office. HQ is in London, and Paris hires travel to London. Transparency. We give direct feedback, and we open the books. Interview process A 20-minute screening call with the CPO: front-end projects, product thinking and how you use AI. A culture fit conversation with a co-founder. A case study on solving a product problem with design and engineering. It may be skipped for some profiles. Why join A new category. Looking after your wealth should be as routine as looking after your health. A real problem. People with $1–20M need far more than investing and savings: taxes, inheritance, children's education, starting companies, cash flow. Unsolved design problems. How people interact with an agent, and how it earns the trust to move their money. There are few precedents to copy. Career growth. One of the first two designers, with a path to Head of Design. A team with a track record. The CEO has built two unicorns, and the team built a consumer social app used by more than 10M people every day. Competitive pay. £100K to £150K base plus equity, both set by level. Send us something you've built and shipped. We'd love to see it! title: Senior TechOps Generalist
description: Seen this advert before? That is because we are continuing to grow! We are very excited to be growing our small and efficient TechOps team at Octopus. We aren't looking for standard IT support - we are looking for an ambitious, deeply knowledgeable and experienced TechOps Generalist to join our team, to grow with the rest of the company, and ensure we are doing so in a secure and safe way. You will be a key partner in defining what TechOps is at Octopus. We will be continuing to shape this team to provide world class support to our employees, building our way out of problems with engineering firepower and undertaking transformational organisational change. We don't just "fix" things - we automate them out of existence. For us, a Generalist isn’t about knowing a little of everything, it’s a multi-disciplinary role for someone who’s deeply experienced in many facets of Enterprise IT. Think multi-domain specialist - not Jack of all trades. What is TechOps? A more modern, more lean version of a traditional enterprise IT team. We cover everything from what most people would call “1st line support” all the way up to high-level strategic planning, and everything in between. We focus on advising rather than enforcing, and give people the autonomy to work with technology to solve their problems in the way that works best for them. We’re an autonomous team who look after a wide range of technology across the business. We empower teams to do the best work they can whilst keeping things running efficiently in the background. We tackle big problems and the breadth of work is huge. Dealing with ambiguity is a key part of working in TechOps, and every day will be a new and exciting one, working on varying challenges across the company. We have a cloud-first approach to everything we do. This allows us to scale quickly and focus on things where we can add the most value. No on-prem AD here! What you'll do Provide delightful day-to-day technical support to all areas of the business, to ensure our incredible employees are able to do their job as efficiently as possible. Their problems are our problems. Troubleshoot and fix a wide range of technical issues, from laptop faults and network issues, to account provisioning failures and SSO problems. Collaborate closely with our Security team to ensure we strike the right balance between security, productivity and user experience. Continually find opportunities to automate our processes and improve the user experience. Empower our people to help themselves by designing and building self-service solutions. Monitor and maintain all the tech in our offices around the world - networks, meeting rooms, printers, digital signage, CCTV, door access control. Managing supplier relationships and the procurement process for SaaS and hardware. Lead and manage complex technical projects with multiple stakeholders from around the business. Examples of some TechOps projects include… Rollout of, and migration to, a new identity provider macOS and Windows MDM migration Rollout of a new device trust and posture compliance solution The replacement of insecure factors like SMS with phishing-resistant factors Office fit-outs, including tech like network, AV, access control etc SaaS migrations for acquisitions e.g. Microsoft 365 to Google Workspace What you'll need We’re looking for people with at least 5-7 years of solid enterprise IT experience. The technical bar is high. While we use Okta, Kandji, Kolide, Zscaler, Meraki and HiBob amongst others, we care about your understanding of the fundamentals of key SaaS tooling, but we also expect candidates to have significant experience implementing and customising these tools for Enterprise environments, so if you’ve lived in Entra and Intune? Awesome! You’ll also need: Confidence in articulating and implementing your technical ability, particularly with enterprise-level SaaS tooling, customer support and automation. The ability to do this both with your peers and novice users is vital. A team player - we don’t want people who vanish and come back with perfect, completed work. You collaborate and work transparently and can identify who can help you, or needs your help. Rich experience and examples of scripting, using APIs to automating mundane and error-prone repetitive tasks. To be comfortable with a huge amount of ambiguity and spinning a lot of plates all at the same time. Experience working with multiple teams and managing multiple stakeholders. Experience managing and deploying macOS, Windows, iOS, and Android at scale Experience administering and troubleshooting Single Sign-On (SSO) technologies such as OAuth, OIDC and SAML. Deep experience with Identity & Access Management. You should be able to explain the nuances of SAML, OIDC, and OAuth , and have hands-on experience with SCIM provisioning. Experience of designing and installing office networks - we use Cisco Meraki. A conscientious approach to everything you do and a passion for doing the right thing rather than the easy thing. Don’t think you check off every single box? We love hiring passionate people with a drive to learn. If you are an expert in some of these areas and are hungry to master the rest, get in touch and let us know where your strengths lie. Why else you'll love it here Octopus Energy Group is a unique culture . An organisation where people learn, decide, and build quicker. Where people work with autonomy, alongside a wide range of amazing co-owners, on projects that break new ground. We want your hard work to be rewarded with perks you actually care about! We won best company to work for in 2022, on Glassdoor we were voted 50 best places to work in 2022 and our Group CEO, Greg has recorded a podcast about our culture and how we empower our people. We’ve also been placed in the top 10 companies for senior leadership Visit our UK perks hub - Octopus Employee Benefits This role can be either fully office based in any of our major offices in Brighton, Manchester, Leicester, Coventry or London , or a hybrid of a few days a week working remotely and office based. #000000;">Investigate opportunities to reduce end-to-end streaming latency across frame capture, buffering, encoding, transport, decoding and presentation. </span></li> </ul> <ul> <li><span style="color: #000000;">Optimise the use and configuration of hardware video encoders, applying knowledge of codec behaviour and low-latency encoding techniques. </span></li> </ul> <ul> <li><span style="color: #000000;">Analyse existing media pipelines to identify unnecessary buffering, memory copies, synchronisation delays and other sources of latency. </span></li> </ul> <ul> <li><span style="color: #000000;">Use software and hardware instrumentation to measure system behaviour, validate hypotheses and quantify the impact of performance changes. </span></li> </ul> <ul> <li><span style="color: #000000;">Investigate and debug issues across user-space applications, system services and daemon-level components. </span></li> </ul> <ul> <li><span style="color: #000000;">Prototype and evaluate new approaches to improving streaming quality, latency and bandwidth efficiency. </span></li> </ul> <ul> <li><span style="color: #000000;">Work with engineers and researchers across the wider organisation on areas such as codec development, rate control, Forward Error Correction and emerging media technologies. </span></li> </ul> <ul> <li><span style="color: #000000;">Contribute technical findings and recommendations to design discussions, working with senior engineers to determine appropriate production solutions. </span></li> </ul> <ul> <li><span style="color: in-person workshops or team events, with travel possible a few times per year. </span></li> </ul> <p style="color: !important;"><span style="color: #000000;"> </span><span style="color: title: Studio Director
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>About Ogilvy  </strong></p> <p>Ogilvy has been creating impact for brands through iconic, culture-changing, value-driving ideas since the company was founded by David Ogilvy more than 75 years ago. It builds on that rich legacy through Borderless Creativity—innovating at the intersection of intelligence, imagination and influence, with experts across advertising, sports & entertainment, PR & social, consulting, and health collaborating seamlessly across more than 120 offices spanning 90 countries. Ogilvy was named <a href="https://www.ogilvy.com/ideas/ogilvy-brings-home-network-year-2026-cannes-lions-international-festival-creativity">Network of the Year</a> at the 2026 Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity and<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span><a href="https://www.ogilvy.com/ideas/ogilvy-tops-warc-effective-100-creative-100-4th-straight-year" data-outlook-id="e2c78315-ff05-4544-925f-9288319dea2c">ranks</a><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>as the #1 global agency network for creative excellence and effectiveness by WARC for the fourth consecutive year, signifying its ability to deliver creative solutions that drive unreasonable impact for clients and communities. Ogilvy is part of WPP, the trusted growth partner for the world's leading brands. Powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform WPP Open, WPP unites cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, creativity, production, enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel.<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>For more information, visit <a href="http://www.ogilvy.com/" target="_blank" data-outlook-id="39833259-880d-4fd8-930f-0d84b1c14850">Ogilvy.com</a>, and follow us on<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span><a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/ogilvy/" data-outlook-id="735e393e-6e8a-4ca8-804a-74f1bd8166b6">LinkedIn</a>, <a href="https://twitter.com/ogilvy" data-outlook-id="d10960ce-761b-48c5-81d5-0a7c4cc6013a">X</a>,<a href="https://www.instagram.com/ogilvy/" data-outlook-id="92ffcb70-6ca7-4d9a-88d5-c130e36e6c4f"> Instagram</a>, and<a href="https://www.facebook.com/ogilvy/" data-outlook-id="3bd2010d-00a2-401b-8cfb-7e8c24deac52"> Facebook.</a></p> <p> </p> <p><strong>About WPP</strong></p> <p>WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. For more information, visit <u><a href="http://wpp.com/" data-outlook-id="7f087527-f491-4cb6-a79d-3b4a67d1ec89">WPP.com</a></u>.</p> <p> </p></div><p style="text-align: center;"><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Studio Director</strong></span></p> <p><strong><br><br>Department: </strong>WPP / Ogilvy<br><strong>Location: </strong>London / National<br><strong>Contract type:</strong> Permanent<br><strong>Full Time/Part time:</strong> Full Time<br><strong>Reporting into:</strong> WPP Lead <br><br></p> <p><strong>The Role</strong><br>As a Studio Director within the Studio Network—a dynamic WPP-operated brand amplification powerhouse—you will be at the helm of creating and scaling distinctive, platform-native content across Europe. Your core mission is to seamlessly run one of our studios, acting as the trusted partner and strategic advisor for brand marketers. You will lead a talented core team, orchestrate creative delivery, and continuously elevate the quality of our output, ensuring our studio remains the go-to destination for every brand brief.</p> <p>At Ogilvy, we are guided by David Ogilvy’s core values: <em>Do the Right Thing, Do the Best Work of Our Lives,</em> and <em>Do It Together.</em> If these principles resonate with you, we’d love for you to join us in shaping what’s next.</p> <p><strong><br>Key Responsibilities</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Lead with Impact:</strong> Direct the studio’s daily operations under the clients leadership, ensuring every brief meets agreed standards and service levels are consistently achieved.</li> <li><strong>Build Lasting Partnerships:</strong> Become the trusted face of the studio to brand marketers across your markets. You'll join their planning sessions, showcase results, and proactively remove any roadblocks.</li> <li><strong>Optimize and Orchestrate:</strong> Smartly match capacity to demand, balancing your core team, flexible resources, and the wider network bench to handle workflow peaks smoothly.</li> <li><strong>Elevate the Creative Standard:</strong> Act as the guardian of quality, overseeing decision gates, tracking compliance to our 100% KPI, and ensuring we hit high scores on the clients Creative Scale.</li> <li><strong>Global Collaboration:</strong> Seamlessly manage the daily workflow with our global delivery centres (India and South Africa), ensuring flawless quality control before assets reach client approvers.</li> <li><strong>Drive Continuous Improvement:</strong> Own the quarterly studio scorecard, pinpointing and driving at least one major operational improvement each quarter.</li> <li><strong>Champion Your Team:</strong> Foster a supportive environment focused on retention and growth. Lead onboarding, ongoing training, and certify the team on every new brand.</li> </ul> <p><strong><br>Key Skills</strong></p> <ul> <li>Proven leadership in running a high-volume, high-quality creative or content studio.</li> <li>Exceptional stakeholder management skills, with a knack for building trust with senior brand marketers and navigating complex matrix structures.</li> <li>Strong operational acumen, including capacity planning, resource management, and workflow optimization across global delivery centres.</li> <li>A sharp eye for creative quality and platform-native content, with experience using data and performance metrics to measure and elevate output.</li> <li>Excellent problem-solving abilities, capable of turning scorecard data into actionable quarterly improvements.</li> <li>A passion for people development, with a track record of building, retaining, and growing high-performing teams.<br><br></li> </ul> <p><strong>About You</strong><br>You are a natural leader who thrives at the intersection of operational excellence and creative brilliance. You don't just manage processes; you inspire teams and build unshakeable trust with clients. You are commercially savvy, culturally fluent, and possess a proactive mindset that spots opportunities for improvement before they become issues. If you are ready to drive an engine that produces world-class content for one of the world's most iconic brand portfolios, and you love seeing your team grow alongside the work, you'll be right at home here.<br><br></p> <p><strong>Benefits & Culture</strong><br>At Ogilvy, we are a friendly, collaborative, and eclectic team united by a shared commitment to doing the best work of our lives. Beyond client work, you’ll have the chance to shape our vibrant culture, join active social teams, and contribute to our industry-leading DEI initiatives.<br><br></p> <p>Here is a snapshot of the benefits we offer:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Hybrid Working:</strong> We embrace a hybrid model that blends collaborative in-office time with the flexibility to work remotely.</li> <li><strong>Annual Leave:</strong> 25 days holiday, a paid volunteering day, plus the option to buy up to 5 additional days.</li> <li><strong>Pension:</strong> a generous matched scheme. Contribute 4% (Ogilvy pays 6%) up to a maximum contribution of 7% (Ogilvy pays 10.5%—totalling a powerful 17.5%).</li> <li><strong>Healthcare & Wellbeing:</strong> BUPA Private Medical Insurance, plus discounted BUPA dental cover or financial contribution towards your physical and mental wellness.</li> <li><strong>Employee Assistance:</strong> 24/7 access to remote GPs, mental health support, physio, nutrition consultations, and confidential counselling for you and your family.</li> <li><strong>Free 1-to-1 Coaching:</strong> Professional and personal growth coaching sessions annually.</li> <li><strong>Life Assurance & Income Protection:</strong> Financial peace of mind for you and your loved ones.</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p>Ogilvy champions innovation and the thoughtful application of AI. We encourage you to use AI tools to enhance your application and achieve the best possible results. During interviews, we may explore how you leverage AI, showcasing your judgment and ability to integrate these technologies effectively.</p> <p>Please ensure your application authentically reflects your own skills, experience, and unique contributions.</p> <p> </p><div class="content-conclusion"><p>At Ogilvy, our people are at the heart of what we do: a creative agency that sparks game-changing ideas across culture and business through collaboration, integrity, and a celebration of self-expression. </p> <p>We believe in building powerful teams with purpose - and we relentlessly curate transformative initiatives that make our commitment to fairness, and equity a reality. </p> <p>Our ultimate mission is to leave a positive impact on the world, creating a better future for all, while supporting and uplifting the global communities we serve.  This is central to our mantra of Borderless Creativity.</p> <p><span data-teams="true">Ogilvy is an equal opportunity employer and considers applicants for all positions without discrimination or regard to particular characteristics. We are committed to fostering a culture of respect in which everyone feels they belong and has the same opportunities to progress in their careers.</span></p> <p>If you need any assistance seeking a job opportunity, or if you need reasonable accommodation with the application process, please contact us at ----- Please note that this contact is only for candidates who are requesting accommodation. Emails for other purposes, including application status requests, will not receive a response.</p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow
